category.name: VBA Macros
category.preferred_workflow: Load or create a DOCM/DOCX file, ensure Document.VbaProject is instantiated, perform module or reference operations through the VbaProject.Collections, validate existence before each change, and save the document with SaveFormat.Docm. Keep each step isolated and avoid assumptions about external resources.

strict_api_bans: Do not reference members that are not present in Aspose.Words 26.11.0.
Do not instantiate VbaReference or VbaModule with unsupported constructors.
Do not create VbaModuleType values that are not defined in the library.
canonical_patterns: Access the VBA project via Document.VbaProject and use its Modules and References collections.
Create VbaModule objects with the parameter-less constructor, then set Name, Type, and SourceCode properties.
Add modules or references using the collection Add method and save the document with SaveFormat.Docm.
nullable_warning_prevention: Check that Document.VbaProject is not null before accessing its collections.
Verify that a VbaModule's SourceCode property is not null before performing string operations.
Confirm that the Modules collection contains items before attempting modifications.

common_failure_patterns.symptom: Compilation fails because the code references members that do not exist in the current Aspose.Words version.
common_failure_patterns.cause: The generator invented API members such as nonexistent constructors or enum values.
common_failure_patterns.fix: Replace invented members with documented Aspose.Words.Vba APIs that are available in version 26.11.0.
common_failure_patterns.prevention: Consult the official API reference and limit code to members that appear in the generated documentation.

common_failure_patterns.symptom: CS1729 errors indicate that VbaModule does not have a constructor accepting arguments.
common_failure_patterns.cause: The code attempted to use overloaded constructors that are not provided by the library.
common_failure_patterns.fix: Instantiate VbaModule with the default constructor and assign Name, Type, and SourceCode properties explicitly.
common_failure_patterns.prevention: Always create VbaModule objects using the parameter-less constructor and set properties after creation.

common_failure_patterns.symptom: CS0117 errors show that VbaModuleType lacks members such as Standard or StandardModule.
common_failure_patterns.cause: The code referenced enum values that were renamed or removed in the current library version.
common_failure_patterns.fix: Use the correct enum members, e.g., VbaModuleType.ProceduralModule or VbaModuleType.ClassModule.
common_failure_patterns.prevention: Reference the enum definition in the Aspose.Words.Vba namespace to select valid values.

common_failure_patterns.symptom: CS0117 and CS1061 errors arise when accessing non-existent VbaReference.Type values or Name property.
common_failure_patterns.cause: The code attempted to filter references using undefined enum members like VbaReferenceType.COM.
common_failure_patterns.fix: Filter references using the supported VbaReferenceType values (e.g., Project) and access available properties such as LibId.
common_failure_patterns.prevention: Review the VbaReference class documentation to use only the properties and enum members that exist.

common_failure_patterns.symptom: Runtime failures occur because the example assumes external files or folders already exist.
common_failure_patterns.cause: The snippet does not create sample documents, modules, or output files before operating on them.
common_failure_patterns.fix: Create deterministic local inputs (e.g., a new Document, sample VbaModule, or temporary output file) within the example.
common_failure_patterns.prevention: Never rely on pre-existing files; always generate required inputs programmatically.

common_failure_patterns.symptom: Runtime errors appear when the code validates unrelated document internals instead of the requested condition.
common_failure_patterns.cause: The validation logic checks properties that are irrelevant to the task, causing false negatives.
common_failure_patterns.fix: Validate only the specific condition required by the task, such as the presence of a VBA project or module count.
common_failure_patterns.prevention: Scope validation to the exact prerequisite of the operation and avoid generic document checks.

narrative.overview: The VBA Macros category illustrates how to work with macro-enabled Word documents using Aspose.Words 26.11.0. Verified snippets demonstrate loading, creating, enumerating, and editing VBA projects, modules, and references while preserving macro integrity.
narrative.purpose: Guide an AI coding agent to produce concise, correct C# examples that manipulate Aspose.Words VBA objects, enforce macro-enabled saving, and respect the documented API surface without introducing unsupported members.
validation_priorities: Validate that a VBA project exists and contains at least one module before any modification.
maintenance_notes: Update examples whenever a new Aspose.Words version changes the VBA API surface to keep the documentation accurate.
